title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Notion
providers.scope_notes: Enterprise for IP restrictions; Business/Enterprise for SAML SSO. Confirm API enforcement and token-expiry requirements with Notion.

controls.name: PAT creation policy (who can create PATs with Notion API access)
controls.what: Limits PAT creation to owners, owners plus selected groups, or all members; removing a member's permission stops their existing PATs.
controls.plan: Business or Enterprise (not configurable on Free/Plus)
controls.quote: If an admin changes the workspace policy so a member is no longer allowed to create PATs with Notion API access, that member's existing PATs stop working for Notion API requests.

controls.name: Revoke personal access tokens
controls.what: Workspace admins revoke any PAT; org owners can list/revoke via the Admin API.
controls.setting: Settings > Connections > All personal access tokens; Admin API
controls.quote: Workspace admins can revoke any PAT in their workspace from Settings → Connections → All personal access tokens.

no_control.what: PAT creation policy is not configurable on Free and Plus plans.
no_control.quote: | Plus | All workspace members. | Not configurable. |

controls_unknown: Whether Notion IP address restrictions apply to internal connection tokens, PATs or public OAuth tokens (help page only describes user sign-in; admin tokens are excluded).
Whether SAML SSO enforcement affects API tokens (not stated).
Whether admins can set a maximum PAT lifetime (creators choose 7 days to 1 year; default 1 year).
Whether internal connection tokens or OAuth tokens expire or can be force-rotated by admins.

authentication.summary: Internal connection tokens, personal access tokens and public-connection OAuth bearer tokens.

federation.details: This path uses a local/static or platform-native credential. Evaluate a separate federation path where listed.

ip_restriction.boundary: Enterprise IP allowlist restricts managed-user sign-in and explicitly does not apply to admin tokens on the admin APIs. Coverage of connection, PAT and OAuth API calls is not documented.

lifetime.summary: Expiry chosen at creation: 7, 30, 90, 180 days or 1 year (default 1 year)

renewal.summary: No refresh. Create a new PAT before expiry; expired tokens return an unauthorized error.

administration.summary: PATs inherit user access. Admins set who may create PATs (plan-dependent), view and revoke workspace PATs; org owners can list/revoke via the Admin API. Removing a member's PAT permission stops their existing PATs.
administration.conditions: Enterprise for IP restrictions; Business/Enterprise for SAML SSO. Confirm API enforcement and token-expiry requirements with Notion.

offboard.details: A PAT acts as its creator and loses access when the creator leaves the workspace.

inventory.details: Admins see all PATs in Settings → Connections; org owners can use the Admin API 'List personal access tokens in a workspace' endpoint.

expiry.ui: Set at creation: Developer portal > Personal access tokens > New token > Expiration. Admin view: Settings → Connections (all PATs)

offboard.ui: Settings → People (or Members) > Members tab > role dropdown > Remove from workspace

token_format.notes: PAT format not documented; Notion treats tokens as opaque. Sent as Authorization: Bearer.

log_sources.name: Settings → Connections → All personal access tokens
log_sources.notes: Admin view of active, expired, revoked PATs; shows creator and revoker.

log_sources.name: Notion Admin API: List personal access tokens
log_sources.notes: Enterprise org bot token with personal-access-token:read; returns created/last-used/revoked metadata.

log_sources.name: Notion workspace audit log
log_sources.notes: Enterprise only; 365-day retention; UI filter by user/integration/agent; IP included where available. API data-access calls are not listed as events.

log_sources.name: Notion SIEM connection (webhook)
log_sources.notes: Enterprise; real-time JSON webhook of every audit log event; payload field names not documented publicly.

credential_id_fields.notes: PAT id; pass as bot_id to revoke
user who created (and acts as) the token

lifecycle_events.notes: who may create PATs changed; disallowed members' PATs stop working for API
PAT use with Notion MCP policy

anomaly_cues: last_used_at recent for a PAT whose creator was deprovisioned or changed role
New PAT created shortly before bulk exports or edits by the creator
PAT with 1-year expiry created by a member who normally has none
Many PATs by one creator (one per tool is advised; sudden growth is odd)
Edits attributed to the creator at times they were not working (PAT acts as the user)

containment.steps: Creator revokes in Developer portal, or admin revokes in Settings → Connections → All personal access tokens, or Admin API DELETE /v1/spaces/{space_id}/personal_access_tokens/{bot_id}. Optionally tighten PAT creation policy.
containment.notes: Revocation is immediate and permanent; token stops working for API and Workers.

sample_query.query: GET https://api.notion.com/admin/v1/spaces/{space_id}/personal_access_tokens  (then filter results where status='active' and last_used_at > incident_start)
sample_query.purpose: List PATs used during the incident window and their creators.

unknown: audit log event for PAT create or revoke (none listed)
PAT API calls in audit log

calls.reveals: for a PAT, the user who created the token (acts with that user's membership and page permissions)
calls.log_notes: Audit log is Enterprise-only; specific logging of /users/me not stated

calls.reveals: pages and data sources the PAT's user can reach
calls.log_notes: Enterprise audit log, 365-day retention; attributed to the PAT's user
Enterprise plan; Page viewed covers reading page data

unknown: Whether PAT reads are logged on non-Enterprise plans (audit log Enterprise-only)
Documented PAT expiry (not found in Notion's own docs)
